content:
Apple Books is my favourite reading application, and it's getting several long-awaited design changes in iOS 27.2. Here's what's new.

Here are the Apple Books changes in iOS 27.2 beta 3

Apple is rolling out several design changes to its Books app, likely in anticipation of the iPhone Duo being an excellent reading device.

iOS 27.2 beta 3 introduces these changes, all centred on the reading experience itself.

While reading a book, iOS 27.2 brings the following design updates:

  • A new progress bar to help you track your reading position
  • The bottom-right menu gets a new three-dot icon and is redesigned as a standard Liquid Glass menu, consistent with other apps
  • Bookmarks have been removed from that menu and moved to the top-right as their own button
  • The "X" button has moved to the top-left
  • The "back" button has moved to the bottom-left and is larger than before

Tim's comment received the most likes

I prefer the Apple Books app over the Kindle app. The Kindle app always feels clunky. I'm glad Apple is paying attention to Books again.

These are only minor updates, but in my experience using the app, they are absolutely welcome improvements.

I've never understood why bookmarks were tucked away in the old menu, so it's great to see them more prominent again. I also really appreciate the new progress bar.

Hopefully if the iPhone Duo does well, Apple will see this as an opportunity to invest more heavily in the Books app. Kindle dominates the e-reader market, but I've always preferred Apple's apps and ecosystem, both for ebooks and audiobooks.

Do you use Apple Books? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments.
